trades.description: An Ornamental Iron Worker builds and installs decorative metal features for buildings and outdoor spaces. They measure, cut, weld, and bolt together railings, stairs, gates, fences, balconies, and window guards, then lift and fasten them into place on site. Their work adds strength, detail, and safety to the places people use every day.

trades.description: A Pointer, Caulker, and Cleaner repairs and protects the outside of buildings, bridges, and chimneys. They scrape out damaged mortar, pack fresh mortar between bricks or stone, seal cracks and joints with caulk, and clean surfaces with water, chemicals, or blasting tools, often from scaffolds. This keeps walls strong, dry, safe, and well maintained.

opportunities.sponsorName: JATC for Bricklayers & Allied Craftworkers, Local Union #3 (Rochester)
opportunities.applicationSummary: Apply online during the recruitment period, print and complete the application, then submit it in person at the JATC office or mail it in. If you cannot print the application, call to have one mailed to you.
opportunities.applicationMailingAddress: BAC LU #3 JATC, 33 Saginaw Drive, Rochester, NY 14623
opportunities.applicationHours: 8:00AM-4:00PM Monday-Friday, excluding legal holidays, to call for a mailed application if you cannot print one.
opportunities.ageRequirement: Must be at least 18 years old at the time of enrollment.
opportunities.transportationRequirement: Must have reliable transportation to and from various job sites and required classes at the approved school.
opportunities.drugTestRequirement: Must pass a physical and a drug test after the offer of employment, at the sponsor's expense, and must submit to random drug testing during the apprenticeship.
opportunities.classRequirement: Must be able to attend required classes at the approved school.
allRequirements: Must be at least 18 years old at the time of enrollment.

Must sign an affidavit stating that they are physically able to perform the work required of the trade, including standing and kneeling for prolonged periods; climbing and working off lifts, ladders, and scaffolds; repetitive bending and stooping; reading blueprints with near vision and using depth perception; verifying alignment of stones, bricks, and blocks with a plumb bob; lifting, carrying, and positioning materials weighing up to 40 pounds; possible exposure to loud noises and respiratory irritants such as dust and chemicals; working in confined spaces and outside in all weather conditions.
Must pass a physical and a drug test, at the sponsor's expense, after the offer of employment.
Must also submit to random drug testing which may be administered at any time during the apprenticeship.
Must provide their own hand tools as appropriate for the trade; estimated cost is approximately $100-$500 depending on the trade.
Must provide proof of employment authorization to work in the United States at the time of offer.
Must have reliable transportation to and from various job sites and required classes at the approved school.
opportunities.requirementsSummary: Applicants must be at least 18, physically able to do the work, have their own hand tools, provide work authorization, pass post-offer physical and drug testing, and have reliable transportation.

trades.description: A Sheet Metal Worker who hangs and rigs signs makes, installs, and secures metal signs, frames, brackets, and supports on buildings or poles. They measure parts, cut and shape sheet metal, use lifts and rigging gear, and bolt or weld signs into place. Their work keeps signs visible, stable, and safer for workers, drivers, and pedestrians.
